response.query: What governance templates (data-use agreements, consent language, role-based access, audit logging) are required to operationalize CARE/IDS protections for sensitive wetland data?
response.answer: To operationalize CARE/IDS protections for sensitive wetland data, use data-use agreements, consent language, role-based access controls, and audit logging. These templates ensure data security and compliance with privacy regulations.

results.content: In FY 2026, EPA will continue to emphasize adherence to statutory requirements and deadlines, including pre-market review of new chemicals, existing chemical evaluations and risk management, data development and collection, review of Confidential Business Information (CBI) claims, and other statutory requirements. • Maintaining the functionality of ChemView, continuing to increase transparency, and expanding the information ChemView makes available to the public, including newly completed chemical assessments, worker protection information, and other new data reported to EPA under TSCA. • (-$14,068.0 / -55.9 FTE) This funding change proposes to eliminate the Lead Risk Reduction Program to deconstruct wasteful spending, reduce unnecessary burden on EPA partners and the regulated community in order to unleash American energy and economic growth, and refocus EPA on its mission. • Implement a targeted UST tribal program, including inspections, enforcement, compliance assistance, and data management, in support of Pillar 1: Clean Air, Land, and Water for Every American of EPA’s Powering the Great American Comeback initiative.

results.title: Estimates for the
results.content: The Agency is currently developing the FY 2026-2030 EPA Strategic Plan, and the FY 2026 Budget will advance the Administrator’s five strategic pillars: Clean Air, Land, and Water for Every American; Restore American Energy Dominance; Engage in Permitting Reform, Cooperative Federalism, and Cross-Agency Partnership; Develop Artificial Intelligence (AI) Capabilities; and Protect American Auto Jobs. The FY 2026 Budget will advance work to implement Executive Order 14154: Unleashing American Energy3 and Executive Order 14162: Putting America First in International Environmental Agreements.4 Clean Air In FY 2026, the Agency will focus on reducing air pollutants and toxics that can cause or exacerbate health issues by working more effectively with states and tribes. As of April 2025, grants awarded by the Program have led to over 159,814 acres of idle land made ready for productive use and over 221,352 jobs and $42 billion leveraged.6 Clean and Safe Water The FY 2026 Budget focuses EPA’s attention on implementing the core environmental statutes of our Nation, including Clean Water Act (CWA), Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA), and Marine Protection, Research and Sanctuaries Act (MPRSA), while also recognizing the need for efficiencies.
